passages.text: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
passages.sermon:
Three men spoke with Job.
These three men stopped answering Job.
Job believed he was righteous.
Job saw himself as right.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁבְּת֡וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָ֭אֵלֶּה מֵעֲנ֣וֹת אֶת־ אִיּ֑וֹב כִּ֤י ה֖וּא צַדִּ֣יק בְּעֵינָֽיו׃פ

passages.text: This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram. He burned with anger against Job for justifying himself rather than God, and he burned with anger against Job’s three friends because they had failed to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.
passages.sermon:
Elihu was the son of Barachel.
Barachel was a Buzite.
Elihu belonged to the family of Ram.
Elihu became very angry.
He was angry with Job.
Job had justified himself instead of God.
Elihu was also angry with Job’s three friends.
The three friends could not answer Job.
They had condemned Job without giving a proper answer.
passages.original: וַיִּ֤חַר אַ֨ף׀ אֱלִיה֣וּא בֶן־ בַּרַכְאֵ֣ל הַבּוּזִי֮ מִמִּשְׁפַּ֪חַ֫ת רָ֥ם בְּ֭אִיּוֹב חָרָ֣ה אַפּ֑וֹ עַֽל־ צַדְּק֥וֹ נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ מֵאֱלֹהִֽים׃ וּבִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת רֵעָיו֮ חָרָ֪ה אַ֫פּ֥וֹ עַ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ מָצְא֣וּ מַעֲנֶ֑ה וַ֝יַּרְשִׁ֗יעוּ אֶת־ אִיּֽוֹב׃

passages.text: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he.
passages.sermon:
Elihu was a man.
Elihu was younger than Job and Job’s three friends.
Elihu waited to speak to Job.
Elihu waited because the other men were older than he was.
passages.original: וֶֽאֱלִיה֗וּ חִכָּ֣ה אֶת־ אִ֭יּוֹב בִּדְבָרִ֑ים כִּ֤י זְֽקֵנִים־ הֵ֖מָּה מִמֶּ֣נּוּ לְיָמִֽים׃

passages.text: But when he saw that the three men had no further reply, his anger was kindled.
passages.sermon:
Elihu was the son of Barachel the Buzite.  
He belonged to the family of Ram.  
Elihu saw the three men.  
The three men had no answer.  
They could not reply.  
Elihu became angry.  
His anger burned.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤רְא אֱלִיה֗וּא כִּ֘י אֵ֤ין מַעֲנֶ֗ה בְּ֭פִי שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיִּ֥חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite declared: “I am young in years, while you are old; that is why I was timid and afraid to tell you what I know.
passages.sermon:
Elihu was the son of Barachel the Buzite.
Elihu spoke to the others.
Elihu said, "I am young."
"You are old."
"Because I am young, I was timid."
"I was afraid to share my knowledge with you."
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַן׀ אֱלִיה֖וּא בֶן־ בַּֽרַכְאֵ֥ל הַבּוּזִ֗י וַיֹּ֫אמַ֥ר צָ֘עִ֤יר אֲנִ֣י לְ֭יָמִים וְאַתֶּ֣ם יְשִׁישִׁ֑ים עַל־ כֵּ֖ן זָחַ֥לְתִּי וָֽאִירָ֓א׀ מֵחַוֺּ֖ת דֵּעִ֣י אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: I thought that age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.
passages.sermon:
Elihu is a young man.
The other men are old.
Elihu thought about wisdom.
He believed older people should speak.
He believed many years should teach wisdom.
He expected age to bring understanding.
passages.original: אָ֭מַרְתִּי יָמִ֣ים יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ וְרֹ֥ב שָׁ֝נִ֗ים יֹדִ֥יעוּ חָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.
passages.sermon:
Elihu is speaking.
Elihu is the son of Barachel the Buzite.
Elihu says that every person has a spirit inside.
God gives this spirit to each person.
The breath of the Almighty gives people understanding.
passages.original: אָ֭כֵן רֽוּחַ־ הִ֣יא בֶאֱנ֑וֹשׁ וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּבִינֵֽם׃

passages.text: It is not only the old who are wise, or the elderly who understand justice.
passages.sermon: Old people are not always wise.\r\nElderly people do not always understand justice.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ רַבִּ֥ים יֶחְכָּ֑מוּ וּ֝זְקֵנִ֗ים יָבִ֥ינוּ מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; I too will declare what I know.’
passages.sermon:
Elihu is a young man.
Elihu speaks to Job and his friends.
Elihu says, "Listen to me."
Elihu says, "I will tell you what I know."
Elihu says, "I also have understanding."
Elihu asks them to pay attention to his words.
passages.original: לָכֵ֣ן אָ֭מַרְתִּי שִׁמְעָה־ לִּ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵּעִ֣י אַף־ אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: Indeed, I waited while you spoke; I listened to your reasoning; as you searched for words, I paid you full attention. But no one proved Job wrong; not one of you rebutted his arguments.
passages.sermon:
I waited while you spoke.
I listened to your reasoning.
You searched for words.
I paid you full attention.
None of you proved Job wrong.
None of you answered his arguments.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן הוֹחַ֨לְתִּי לְֽדִבְרֵיכֶ֗ם אָ֭זִין עַד־ תְּב֥וּנֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם עַֽד־ תַּחְקְר֥וּן מִלִּֽין׃ וְעָֽדֵיכֶ֗ם אֶתְבּ֫וֹנָ֥ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵ֣ין לְאִיּ֣וֹב מוֹכִ֑יחַ עוֹנֶ֖ה אֲמָרָ֣יו מִכֶּֽם׃

passages.text: So do not claim, ‘We have found wisdom; let God, not man, refute him.’
passages.sermon:
Do not say, “We have found wisdom.”
Do not claim that you are wise.
God must refute Job.
A man cannot refute Job.
Let God answer him, not a person.
passages.original: פֶּן־ תֹּ֣֭אמְרוּ מָצָ֣אנוּ חָכְמָ֑ה אֵ֖ל יִדְּפֶ֣נּוּ לֹא־ אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: But Job has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
passages.sermon: Job has not spoken his words against me.\r\nI will not answer him using your arguments.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ עָרַ֣ךְ אֵלַ֣י מִלִּ֑ין וּ֝בְאִמְרֵיכֶ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Job’s friends are dismayed, with no more to say; words have escaped them.
passages.sermon:
Job’s friends feel dismayed.
They do not answer anymore.
They have no more words to speak.
Words have left them.
passages.original: חַ֭תּוּ לֹא־ עָ֣נוּ ע֑וֹד הֶעְתִּ֖יקוּ מֵהֶ֣ם מִלִּֽים׃

passages.text: Must I wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand and no longer reply?
passages.sermon:
Job’s friends have stopped speaking.
They stand in silence.
They do not answer anymore.
Should I keep waiting?
They remain silent and do not reply.
passages.original: וְ֭הוֹחַלְתִּי כִּי־ לֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ כִּ֥י עָ֝מְד֗וּ לֹא־ עָ֥נוּ עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: I too will answer; yes, I will declare what I know.
passages.sermon:
Job’s friend speaks now.
He sees that Job’s friends are silent.
They have no more words.
He decides to answer too.
He will give his own reply.
He will declare what he knows.
passages.original: אַעֲנֶ֣ה אַף־ אֲנִ֣י חֶלְקִ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵעִ֣י אַף־ אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: For I am full of words, and my spirit within me compels me.
passages.sermon:
Elihu is speaking.
Elihu is a young man.
Elihu is addressing Job and Job’s friends.
I am full of words.
My spirit is inside me.
My spirit compels me to speak.
passages.original: כִּ֭י מָלֵ֣תִי מִלִּ֑ים הֱ֝צִיקַ֗תְנִי ר֣וּחַ בִּטְנִֽי׃

passages.text: Behold, my belly is like unvented wine; it is about to burst like a new wineskin.
passages.sermon:
Elihu is speaking.
Elihu is a young man.
Elihu is full of words.
Elihu feels compelled to speak.
Elihu says, “Look at me.”
“My belly is like wine that has no vent.”
“My belly is ready to burst.”
“My belly is like a new wineskin that is about to break.”
passages.original: הִנֵּֽה־ בִטְנִ֗י כְּיַ֥יִן לֹא־ יִפָּתֵ֑חַ כְּאֹב֥וֹת חֲ֝דָשִׁ֗ים יִבָּקֵֽעַ׃

passages.text: I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and respond.
passages.sermon:
I must speak now.
I need relief.
I will open my lips.
I will give my answer.
passages.original: אֲדַבְּרָ֥ה וְיִֽרְוַֽח־ לִ֑י אֶפְתַּ֖ח שְׂפָתַ֣י וְאֶֽעֱנֶֽה׃

passages.text: I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man.
passages.sermon: I will not show favoritism to any person.\r\nI will not flatter any man.
passages.original: אַל־ נָ֭א אֶשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי־ אִ֑ישׁ וְאֶל־ אָ֝דָ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲכַנֶּֽה׃

passages.text: For I do not know how to flatter, or my Maker would remove me in an instant.
passages.sermon: I do not know how to flatter.\r\nGod is my Maker.\r\nIf I flatter, God will remove me at once.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֲכַנֶּ֑ה כִּ֝מְעַ֗ט יִשָּׂאֵ֥נִי עֹשֵֽׂנִי׃
